The challenge: too many competing priorities and decisions that live only in conversations.

WORKING PRINCIPLE
Keep the first version simple. A completed one-page plan is more useful than an elaborate plan that is never used.
Your working output: Customer conversations completed, plus a short record of the decisions behind it.

content.heading: THE FIVE-PART METHOD
content.subheading: Move from intention to a repeatable practice.
body: 1. Set the direction - Write one measurable outcome, a time horizon and the reason it matters.
2. Understand the context - Capture customer needs, current capacity, constraints and available evidence.
3. Choose the priority - Compare options by impact, effort, risk and reversibility; select the smallest useful move.
4. Assign ownership - Name the decision owner, next action, resources, milestone and review date.
5. Review the evidence - Check progress against the agreed measure, record learning and adjust the plan.
USE THE METHOD IN ORDER
Do not skip the context step. A decision made without understanding constraints often creates rework.
Keep evidence, assumptions and open questions separate. Revisit assumptions when new information arrives.

content.heading: GUIDED WORKSHEET
content.subheading: Write it down. Make the next step visible.
body: WORKSHEET: BUSINESS MODEL CANVAS WORKBOOK
1. OUTCOME - What should be different when this work is complete?
2. CURRENT POSITION - What is true today? What evidence do you have?
3. PEOPLE / AUDIENCE - Who is affected, involved or making the decision?
4. CONSTRAINTS - What limits time, budget, energy, information or capacity?
5. PRIORITY - What is the most useful next move, and why now?
6. SUPPORT - What resource, permission or conversation would help?
7. SUCCESS SIGNAL - Which of these matters most: Customer conversations completed, Priority milestones delivered, Decisions closed on time, Operating issues resolved?
8. REVIEW DATE - When will you pause, check evidence and decide what changes?
